references.text: The Letter to the Hebrews mentions the jar of manna that was kept in the ark of the covenant, as a fulfillment of the command to preserve an omer of manna for future generations.
The following verses describe how Aaron carried out the command by placing the manna before the Testimony for safekeeping.
The description of the ark of the covenant where the manna was to be kept, as a testimony for future generations.
Moses reminds the people how God fed them with manna in the wilderness, which they and their fathers had not known.
A reminder that God gave them manna in the wilderness, which their fathers did not know.
A parallel to the keeping of holy objects before the Testimony as a sign for future generations.
Jesus refers to the manna that the fathers ate in the wilderness and explains that it was the Father who gave the bread from heaven.
Jesus compares himself with the manna and declares that he is the true bread from heaven that gives eternal life.
The psalm describes how God caused manna to rain down on the people and gave them the grain of heaven to eat.
Nehemiah reminds how God gave manna to the people in the wilderness and withheld nothing from them.
Both verses establish a memorial ritual (the manna versus unleavened bread) intended to preserve the memory of the exodus from Egypt for coming generations.
Verse 16:4 is the original command concerning the manna, which the source verse (16:32) later instructs should be kept as a memorial.
Verse 16:15 describes the discovery of the manna, which the source verse (16:32) later commands should be preserved for future generations.
